subject: "Error: Convergence issue" vs. "Warning: LL not replicated"

messages.author: 994ec6b94f9fe8c9
messages.subject: "Error: Convergence issue" vs. "Warning: LL not replicated"
parts:
Good morning!  

I'm a PhD candidate at UW-Madison and I have been using the compare_solutions_mplus function in tidyLPA to compare solutions for four indicators.  I'm hoping to get some clarification on the difference between the result "Error:Convergence issue" and "Warning: LL not replicated." My understanding is that LL not replicated indicates that a local solution was reached.  The advice I have seen for this warning is to increase the number of random starts or put the indicators on the same scale.  I'm wondering what "Error: Convergence issue" is indicative of, so that I can determine how to address. 

Thanks for any clarification you may be able to provide!

Christine Anhalt-Depies
anhalt...@wisc.edu

messages.author: ad4ca8f2f2ac1feb
messages.subject: Re: "Error: Convergence issue" vs. "Warning: LL not replicated"
parts:
You are correct in that when the LL is not replicated that your model may have converged on a local maximum, and it is not recommended to use a solution where the LL is not replicated.  Increasing the number of random starts, increasing the number of final optimizations, and increasing the number of st_iterations may all help the LL to replicate. 

The "Error: Convergence issue"  means the model was unable to find a solution using your input parameters.  This generally indicates that the model/profile solution is not a good fit for the data, and it may be a good idea to look at other model/profile solutions.

I hope that helps!

messages.author: 3cfaef29dbc536f8
messages.subject: Re: "Error: Convergence issue" vs. "Warning: LL not replicated"
parts:
You may have a little better luck searching expectation-maximization - that is the algorithm for finding the maximum likelihood estimates underlying mlcust and MPlus.

My understanding is that this issue *generally* means there's not an easily-found solution. It doesn't mean there isn't one but it may suggest that there are a number of comparable, possible solutions. It seems sensible that outliers may cause an issue; less clear to me why repetitions in the data, though we have encountered some issues in our work where values that are not truly continuous (for variables with, for example, possible values of 1, 2, 3, and 4 - not all of the values between 1 and 4, or any values between a wider range) have caused issues.

I'd focus on trying to increase the number of iterations first- see how that goes. You can also try one of the other model specifications.

Hope this helps.
